cues.en: Let's now have a look at why and when we need a firewall.
And I would like to start this lecture with a few common myths about firewalls.
So the first question would be, does a firewall protect my PC from the Internet?
And usually the answer here is no.
A firewall just allows us to define custom rules for network traffic and how that should be handled.
And usually when we set up a firewall, we mostly or we only define rules for incoming network traffic.
I'm saying mostly here because we might also want to limit our outgoing traffic, but most of the time
we want to define rules for incoming network traffic.
Aside from minor exceptions, for example, file sharing, BitTorrent or things like that, most applications
don't allow incoming traffic anyway and they are not responding to it.
So that means, for example, if we are running a browser like Firefox and we connect to websites,
Firefox isn't allowing incoming connections anyway, it's only building up connections from our Firefox
to a remote server.
So for our personal computer where we are running our Ubuntu or our desktop Linux on there, not that
many services that are available or accessible from the outside world anyway.
And usually we then for example, we don't want to limit then outgoing traffic because maybe we could
block a few websites that are malicious, but we might just miss one.

that's already we can already access that one and.
If we were to execute code from there.
Maybe because we download a file that we then execute manually.
Well then we have already executed it and our firewall doesn't protect us anymore.
Also, we are usually behind a network address translation without port forwarding.
If we are using IPV four or incoming traffic is blocked by our router anyway, that would be IPV six.
But in both cases people on the internet can't just connect to our computer because usually there's
a router in between that will just block this traffic.
So it's not like our computer can just be accessed from the internet and there are open ports there.
If we are in a normal home network, it might be different if we are on a server and there are a lot
of services running there.
But on a normal PC, a firewall is not that necessary.
The next thing is whether we can use a firewall to completely go silent in the sense that we can just
block all incoming traffic.

there.
